To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the asymptotic behavior of SRPT and FBPS/PS is different for medium size jobs, the SRPT discipline is asymptotically optimal for small jobs, and the proposed comparison grouping mechanism is asymptotically close to the performance of the SRPT discipline for medium size jobs.

the conditional sojoun time distributions of the studied scheduling disciplines exhibit heavy tails, and that the asymptotic performance for relatively smaller jobs is considerably better for SRPT than for PS/FBSP.

(i) SRPT is asymptotically optimal among the considered disciplines for relatively smaller jobs, (ii) the asymptotic performance difference between PS/FBPS and SRPT is large enough to justify the additional complexity of SRPT, (iii) the comparison scheduling mechanism is a good approximation of SRPT, and (iv) the performance difference between SRPT and the comparison scheduling mechanism can be reduced significantly by using more than two classes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel asymptotic analysis of medium sized job arrivals in heavy-traffic, where the job sizes are modeled as Pareto distributed random variables.
a new class of scheduling disciplines that are based on relative job size comparison.
the development of a novel methodology for the performance analysis of the scheduling disciplines in the heavy-tailed environment, which is based on a new conditional limit approach.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SRPT exhibits a much better behavior than FBPS for relatively smaller jobs and that the SRPT-based comparison grouping mechanism is an efficient way to approximate SRPT for medium size jobs.

the proposed SRPT comparison scheduling mechanism exhibits a superior performance in terms of the sojourn times and the average waiting times compared to PS, FBPS and SRPT, for a broad class of job requirement distributions.
the SRPT discipline exhibits better performance than the PS/FBPS disciplines for small jobs and, in turn, PS/FBPS outperform SRPT for relatively large jobs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed an asymptotic theory to compare the conditional limits for the sojourn times of PS/FBPS and SRPT scheduling disciplines under the condition that the job size is smaller than exactly some fixed number out of the preceding arrivals.

the SRPT discipline is the only scheduling policy among the considered disciplines that is able to achieve the optimal asymptotic performance in the sense of heavy-tailed job sizes, and that the comparison scheduling can provide an effective approximation to the optimal asymptotic behavior of SRPT.
we introduce a novel notion of conditional limits and use them to analyze the asymptotic performance behavior of PS/FBPS and SRPT disciplines.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the asymptotic analysis of the conditional limits can be used as a tool for the performance evaluation of the proposed comparison scheduling mechanism.
the SRPT scheduling discipline, which is known to be optimal for the mean waiting time criterion under heavy-tailed traffic, can be efficiently approximated using the comparison grouping mechanism.
, for the medium size job classes, the SRPT discipline can be approximated with high accuracy by the comparison scheduling with a relatively small number of classes.
